title: One thing I know (John 9:13–41)
hookLine: whereas I was blind, now I see

cards: The man has barely begun to see when the questions start. He's questioned by religious authorities, then questioned again. His parents are summoned, and they're too frightened to speak for him.

By the end he has been thrown out. The healing takes two verses; the argument about it fills the rest of the chapter, and it's mostly a trial. And the man who used to beg by the road turns out to have a sharp tongue.

teach.b: The healing happened on a Sabbath, and the Pharisees are divided. Some say a man who doesn't keep the Sabbath can't be from God; others ask how a sinner could do such signs.
They call the man back and press him: give glory to God; we know this man is a sinner.
He answers, in the Douay-Rheims: "If he be a sinner, I know not: one thing I know, that whereas I was blind, now I see." He doesn't argue theology or claim to know everything.

teach.h: A NAME, A PROPHET, FROM GOD, LORD.
teach.b: He knows one thing, from the inside. When they ask him to tell it all again, he asks, with a straight face, whether they want to become his disciples too. Watch him grow through the chapter.
At first, Jesus is the man that is called Jesus. Then a prophet. Then a man from God.
They put him out, and Jesus, hearing of it, goes looking for him and asks if he believes in the Son of God.
Who is he, Lord, that I may believe? You have seen him, Jesus says, and it is he that talketh with thee. "And he said: I believe, Lord. And falling down, he adored him."
Some readers think the fear of being put out of the synagogue also reflects painful conflicts in the communities John was writing for.

teach.h: WHEREAS I WAS BLIND, NOW I SEE.
teach.b: The Church reads the chapter as a story about sight that grows: the one who was blind sees more and more, and those sure they could see are asked whether they really do.

how: Catholics hear the whole of John 9, the trial as well as the healing, in the longer form of the Gospel on the Fourth Sunday of Lent in Year A.

games.q: what does “one thing i know” mean?
o: a polite way of refusing to answer at all
holding to what you've seen, without every answer
a proud claim to know more than the teachers

games.q: one thing I know — tap the pairs.
p: the man that is called Jesus
too frightened to speak for him

s: the Pharisees all agreed against Jesus
they were divided: some asked how a sinner could do such signs.
the man claimed to understand who Jesus was right away
he said one thing I know. his understanding grew through the day.
after he was put out, Jesus went looking for him
and the man said: I believe, Lord.

games.q: you were blind this morning. now authorities press you: we know this man is a sinner. what do you say?
o: I don't know about that; one thing I know: I was blind, now I see.
games.why: "If he be a sinner, I know not: one thing I know, that whereas I was blind, now I see." he speaks only of what he knows.

practice: Think back over the past few months, on this path or in your life, and find one thing you see now that you didn't before, about a person, about yourself, about God.
Say it plainly to yourself, the way he did: whereas I was blind, now I see this. If you pray, give thanks for it; if not, just let it be named.

wordCard.voice: One thing I know. The healed man's answer to his questioners: I don't know everything, but whereas I was blind, now I see. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: now I see. That's week seventy-three: words of eternal life, rivers, light, truth, I am, Siloe, and one thing I know.
